body.asks: The author's word of 2026-11-11: he does not know yet how helpful Fable is; at the next reading for faults one Fable and one Opus read the same piece and their findings are compared, and if Fable's are not drastically more significant, Fable is not used for now. How a session works names Fable the peer until this is settled.

What Fable found reading the git reader, still to mend; mended on 2026-11-11 in Mending the edges: a folder that is no repository refused in words, an unborn HEAD read as none, an annotated tag peeled to its commit, a ref and an object each built in one place, git asked in plain words. Left: every read spawns git, so a read costs about 150 ms and a whole minutes, wanting one long-lived cat-file; ref and type ids by name collide across repositories, waiting on a root; a submodule's entry holds what is not there; the tip is HEAD's tree only by order; all() spawns once per step where git log and ls-tree would do in two; a moving ref shows no new version; a tag of a tag may peel one level only on older git, and a lightweight tag on a tree or blob puts what is no commit under commit.
